message.content:
I need to find where memo-related derived metadata is computed from memo content in this repository. This metadata is used for lists/previews and is computed automatically rather than set by the user.

Search breadth: very thorough

Look for:
1. Any "memo" related models, stores, or services that compute/derive metadata from content
2. Functions that extract properties like title, snippet, summary, description from memo content
3. Any memo-related code that parses or processes content to generate preview/list data

Search in all relevant directories - this could be in a server/API layer, a store, a service, or a shared utility. Check for patterns like "extractMeta", "computeMeta", "parseMemo", "memoMeta", "snippet", "excerpt", etc.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

## Findings: Memo-Derived Metadata Computation

This repository (the "Memos" project) computes derived metadata from memo content in two distinct ways: **payload properties** (persisted to the database) and **snippet** (computed on-the-fly at serving time). All computation happens server-side in Go; the frontend consumes these as read-only `OUTPUT_ONLY` fields.

---

### 1. Proto Definitions (the schema for derived metadata)

**`/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto`** (lines 7-22)
Defines `MemoPayload.Property` -- the persisted metadata stored alongside each memo:
- `has_link` (bool) -- whether the memo content contains a markdown link
- `has_task_list` (bool) -- whether the memo has task list checkboxes
- `has_code` (bool) -- whether the memo has code blocks or inline code
- `has_incomplete_tasks` (bool) -- whether the memo has unchecked task items
- `title` (string) -- the title extracted from the first H1 heading, if present

**`/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`** (lines 256, 265-266, 272-278)
Defines the API-facing representation:
- `property` (field 15) -- the computed properties above, marked `OUTPUT_ONLY`
- `snippet` (field 17) -- a plain-text snippet of the memo content, marked `OUTPUT_ONLY`
- `tags` (field 10) -- tags extracted from content, marked `OUTPUT_ONLY`

---

### 2. Core Extraction Engine

**`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`**

This is the central file where all metadata derivation from memo content happens. It implements the `Service` interface using the [goldmark](https://github.com/yuin/goldmark) markdown parser. Key methods:

- **`ExtractAll`** (lines 356-422) -- The primary single-pass extraction function. Parses the markdown AST once and extracts:
  - **Tags**: Finds all `#tag` nodes (via custom `TagNode` AST type), deduplicates them
  - **Mentions**: Finds all `@mention` nodes (via custom `MentionNode` AST type), lowercased and deduped
  - **Property.Title**: If the very first block-level child of the document is an H1 heading, extracts its plain text
  - **Property.HasLink**: Set `true` if any `Link` node exists
  - **Property.HasCode**: Set `true` if any `CodeBlock`, `FencedCodeBlock`, or `CodeSpan` node exists
  - **Property.HasTaskList**: Set `true` if any `TaskCheckBox` node exists
  - **Property.HasIncompleteTasks**: Set `true` if any unchecked `TaskCheckBox` exists

- **`GenerateSnippet`** (lines 264-346) -- Creates a plain-text preview by walking the AST:
  - Extracts text from `Text` nodes, `AutoLink` nodes, and `TagNode` nodes
  - Skips code blocks (but keeps inline code spans)
  - Adds spacing between block-level elements (paragraphs, headings, list items, table cells)
  - Truncates at a word boundary using `truncateAtWord` (lines 472-489) when exceeding `maxLength` (typically 64 characters)

- **`ExtractProperties`** (lines 193-241) -- Standalone property extraction (same logic as in `ExtractAll` but for isolated use)

- **`ExtractTags`** (lines 143-170) -- Standalone tag extraction

Helper functions:
- **`extractHeadingText`** (lines 173-179) -- Recursively extracts plain text from a heading node (strips formatting like bold/italic)
- **`truncateAtWord`** (lines 472-489) -- Truncates at last word boundary, handles multi-byte UTF-8 (rune-based counting)

---

### 3. Where Metadata Is Computed and Persisted

**`/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`**

- **`RebuildMemoPayload`** (lines 74-88) -- Called to rebuild a memo's payload from its content. Calls `markdownService.ExtractAll()` and stores the resulting `Tags` and `Property` into `memo.Payload`.
- **`Runner.RunOnce`** (lines 27-72) -- Batch rebuilds payload for ALL memos (used for migration/maintenance). Processes memos in batches of 100.

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`**

- **On memo creation** (line 108): `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService)` is called before persisting the memo.
- **On memo update** (line 447): When the `content` field is in the update mask, `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, s.MarkdownService)` is called to recompute tags and properties, and the updated payload is saved.

---

### 4. Where Snippet Is Computed (at serving time, not persisted)

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`** (lines 83-90)

- **`getMemoContentSnippet`** -- Calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet(content, 64)` to produce a 64-character-max plain-text snippet.

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`**

- **`convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators`** (line 76-80) -- During memo-to-API conversion, calls `getMemoContentSnippet` and sets `memoMessage.Snippet`.
- **`convertMemoPropertyFromStore`** (lines 315-326) -- Converts the stored `MemoPayload_Property` to the API `Memo_Property` (a direct mapping of `HasLink`, `HasTaskList`, `HasCode`, `HasIncompleteTasks`, `Title`).
- **`batchConvertMemoRelations`** (lines 173-288) -- When loading relations, optionally generates snippets for related memos to populate `MemoRelation.Memo.Snippet` and `MemoRelation.RelatedMemo.Snippet`.

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go`** (lines 318-328)

- **`memoNotificationSnippet`** -- Generates snippet for notification payloads (inbox/email).

---

### 5. Markdown Service Initialization

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go`** (lines 48-51)

The production markdown service is created with both extensions enabled:
```go
markdownService := markdown.NewService(
    markdown.WithTagExtension(),
    markdown.WithMentionExtension(),
)
```

---

### 6. Frontend Usage (consumption only, no derivation)

The frontend does **not** compute any derived metadata itself. It consumes the server-provided fields:

- **`/bench/repo/web/src/types/proto/api/v1/memo_service_pb.ts`** (lines 186-190) -- TypeScript type with `snippet: string` field
- **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoView/components/MemoSnippetLink.tsx`** -- Renders snippet in relation links
- **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoDetailSidebar/MemoDetailSidebar.tsx`** (line 155) -- Uses `relatedMemo.snippet` for relation sidebar display
- **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/UserMemoMap/UserMemoMap.tsx`** (line 154) -- Uses `memo.snippet` in map popups

---

### Summary

The derived metadata pipeline is:

1. **Content arrives** (create or update a memo)
2. **`RebuildMemoPayload`** in `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` calls `markdownService.ExtractAll()` to derive `Tags`, `Property.Title`, `Property.HasLink`, `Property.HasCode`, `Property.HasTaskList`, `Property.HasIncompleteTasks` -- these are **persisted** in the database as part of `memo.Payload`
3. **At serving time**, `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators` in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` calls `getMemoContentSnippet()` (which calls `markdownService.GenerateSnippet(content, 64)`) to produce the plain-text **snippet** -- this is **computed on-the-fly**, not stored
4. Both `property` and `snippet` are returned as `OUTPUT_ONLY` fields in the API response
